revisions.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit f37240a9ae: Update EIP-7892: harden the spec with p2p details.
revisions.summary: Largest single expansion of the EIP. Adds author Raul Kripalani (@raulk). Restructures the Specification into Definition / Blob schedule configuration / Execution layer configuration / Consensus layer configuration subsections. Execution layer: each blobSchedule fork is now linked to activation via a top-level `<fork_name>Time` Unix-timestamp field, BPO forks SHOULD be named `bpo<index>` starting at 1, activation timestamps are required only for post-Prague forks, and the illustrative JSON switches from raw-timestamp keys to named osaka/bpo1/bpo2 entries plus cancunTime/pragueTime/osakaTime/bpo1Time/bpo2Time. Adds the rule that a regular hardfork changing these parameters MUST do so by adding a blob schedule entry. Consensus layer: `BLOB_SCHEDULE` is defined as the sequence of blob-parameter changes after ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH, one entry per changing fork. Adds a modified `compute_fork_digest` taking `current_epoch` and `blob_schedule` and XOR-bitmasking `max_blobs_per_block` into the 4-byte digest (returning the base digest when no schedule entry applies). Adds a P2P Networking section: a new ENR entry `nfd` (SSZ Bytes4 ForkDigest, 'next fork digest') that nodes MUST evaluate alongside ENRForkID::next_* fields, a note that `Status` req/resp is unchanged but must carry the updated fork_digest, and a note that gossip topics rotate automatically at a BPO fork. Drops the earlier requirement 'BPO forks MUST NOT conflict with other fork schedules' and changes 'The timestamp in blobSchedule' to 'The slot number in the EL's blobSchedule'.

revisions.summary: Largest redesign of the response. Removes the six hash/fork-id top-level members (`currentHash`/`nextHash`/`lastHash`, `currentForkId`/`nextForkId`/`lastForkId`) so the response contains exactly three members `current`, `next`, `last`, with `next`/`last` null when no future fork is configured. Deletes the 'Converting a Fork Configuration to a Hash' section (RFC-8785 canonicalization plus CRC-32) and replaces the 'CRC-32 as Hash Format' rationale with 'Why no configuration hash'. Adds a per-configuration `forkId` member (EIP-6122 FORK_HASH, `0x`-prefixed, zero-padded to four bytes, lower case). Renames the member `blobsSchedule` -> `blobSchedule` (including in the BPO section). Inverts the `precompiles` object so members are contract names and values are addresses, and requires members in alphabetical rather than 'canonical' order, with the rule that future forks' added members MUST be alphabetically sorted. Rewrites all sample configurations accordingly and adds a 'Without Future Fork Scheduled' example returning `next: null` and `last: null`. Weakens DDoS guidance from 'Clients SHOULD cache' to 'Clients MAY cache'.
